findings.description: split appends an extra trailing empty string whenever s ends with the delimiter. Under the installed Magma (V2.29-8), Split(s,d:IncludeEmpty) ALREADY includes the trailing empty element (the code comment 'which Split omits' describes older Magma behavior), so the manual 'cat [""]' duplicates it. Consequence: split violates its documented python r.split(d) semantics, and getrecs (line 107, built on split) mis-parses every record line ending in the delimiter -- i.e. any data file whose last column is empty gains a spurious extra column, and putrecs/getrecs no longer round-trip. Since getrecs is the package's core reader for LMFDB-style colon-delimited files, this silently corrupts downstream parsing. Also, split crashes on the empty string (s[#s] indexes out of range) whereas python ''.split(d) == [''].

Same Magma-version drift as split (line 102): Split(s,c:IncludeEmpty) now already includes the trailing empty string, so the manual Append(~t,"") when s ends with c produces one EXTRA copy of the replacement string d at the end of the output. ReplaceCharacter("a:",":","XY") returns "aXYXY" instead of "aXY", contradicting the docstring 'replace every occurrence of the character c in s with the string d'. Also crashes on the empty string s (s[#s] out of range) instead of returning "".

The docstring promises the Zagier extension H(-u^2) = -u/2 for negative arguments, but the code tests IsSquare(N) with N < 0, which is always false over the integers, so HurwitzClassNumber(N) returns 0 for EVERY N < 0 and the -u/2 branch is dead code. Correct behavior per the documented convention (used in Eichler-Selberg/Hurwitz-Kronecker trace-formula boundary terms): HurwitzClassNumber(-1) = -1/2, HurwitzClassNumber(-4) = -1, HurwitzClassNumber(-9) = -3/2. The test should be IsSquare(-N). Note mfdims.m's H12(N) explicitly forwards N le 0 to this intrinsic (mfdims.m:313), so any future negative-square call from the trace-formula code (e.g. the H12(-d) call inside the function newersz1p marked 'currently broken' at mfdims.m:1036) silently gets 0; positive arguments are unaffected (verified against the Eichler mass relation).

atoiiii validates the whitespace-stripped copy t (line 259/263) but then parses the ORIGINAL unstripped s (line 264: s := s[2..#s-1]). All sibling parsers (atoii, atoiii) strip whitespace before parsing. With interior whitespace the delimiter scan Index(s,"]],[[" ) fails to match "]], [[" and the input is SILENTLY mis-parsed at the wrong nesting depth: atoiiii("[[[1]], [[2]]]") returns [[[1],[2]]] instead of [[[1]],[[2]]] -- wrong shape, no error.

getval is declared for X::Any and documented as the analog of Python's get, but 'b,v := IsDefined(X,k)' assumes the two-return-value form of IsDefined, which only exists for associative arrays. For a SeqEnum (or any indexable type whose IsDefined returns a single boolean) it crashes with 'Expected 2 values for where identifiers but only computed 1 value(s)' instead of returning X[k]/missing. Internal package use (IndexFibers) only passes Assoc so it works there, but the documented general contract is broken.

When the smallest input partition has a single block (k eq 1), the code returns S[1] itself -- a SetMulti[RngIntElt] -- instead of a set of partitions {S[1]}, contradicting the declared return type SetEnum[SetMulti[RngIntElt]] and the behavior of every other return path (compare line 635 which correctly returns {{*&+S[1]*}} and line 624 which returns Set(S)). A caller iterating over the result then iterates over the integers of the partition rather than over partitions.

atoiii handles the empty-list-of-lists forms "[]" and "[[]]" and handles an empty tuple mixed with others ("[<1>,<>]" works), but the lone empty tuple "[<>]" (length 4) trips 'assert #t gt 4' and crashes, even though the tuple branch below would parse it correctly (the a[1] eq ">" special case exists precisely for "<>"). "[<>]" is exactly what sprint produces for [<>] / a sequence containing one empty tuple.

findings.description: OUT OF MY ASSIGNED RANGE (flagging so it is not missed): gl2tab.m line 33 defines colsplit := func<s|Split(s,":":IncludeEmpty) cat (s[#s] eq ":" select [""] else [])>, a copy of the same trailing-empty double-append pattern as utils.m split (line 102). findings.description: The entire GF(p) branch (lines 859-880) indexes inv[5] and in one spot builds 5-element result vectors, but Magma's IgusaClebschInvariants returns exactly 4 invariants [I2,I4,I6,I10] (weights [1,2,3,5]). The branch was copy-pasted from the 5-invariant NormalizedIgusaInvariants (lines 890-923) without re-indexing, so EVERY code path crashes with an index-out-of-range error for any genus 2 curve over GF(p), p>2: line 864 (I2!=0 case), lines 867-868 (I4!=0 case), line 872 (I6!=0 case, which also builds a 5-entry vector [0,0,r,c^4*inv[4],c^5*inv[5]] inconsistent with the 4-entry vectors on lines 875-876), and line 879 (returns a 5-entry vector [0,0,0,0,...]). Additionally line 873 says 'return inv' (raw un-normalized invariants) where the parallel Igusa code (line 904) correctly says 'return inv1'. Correct behavior: normalize [I2,I4,I6,I10] with weights [1,2,3,5], i.e. slot 4 is c^5*inv[4]. I implemented the fix below as a standalone function and verified exhaustively for p in {3,5,7,11,13} over ALL nonzero invariant vectors in F_p^4 that it (a) returns a vector in the weighted scaling orbit of the input and (b) is constant on orbits (canonical); also verified on curves (quadratic twists over GF(5)/GF(11) map to equal output).

The doubled-power list is built with 'while q lt B', so the element q = B is omitted when B is exactly p^(2^k) (k>=1) for some p in P. Since subset products of {p, p^2, p^4, ...} represent exponents in binary, B = p^(2^k) can only be represented using the element B itself, so the count is silently short by exactly 1 for every such B (the docstring says 'positive integers <= B', inclusive). Correct behavior: include q = B, i.e. 'while q le B'.

Same bug as SmoothNumberCount (the two intrinsics share the copy-pasted list construction): 'while q lt B' omits q = B, so the returned list is missing the value B itself whenever B = p^(2^k) (k>=1, p in P), contradicting the docstring 'integers in [B0,B]' (inclusive).

Docstring states 'returns a list of integers z and a nonzero rational number r such that z[i] = v[i]*r^w[i] for all i', but the code (line 850: z := [Integers()|v[i]*r^(-w[i]):i in [1..#v]]) returns r with z[i] = v[i]*r^(-w[i]), i.e. the exponent sign is inverted (equivalently the returned r is the inverse of the documented one). The sign-flip step (line 852) is consistent with the r^(-w) convention (z := [(-1)^w[i]*z[i]], r := -r), so the code is self-consistent and only the docstring is wrong.
findings.evidence:
> z,r,b := NormalizedProjectiveInvariants([8/3,4/9],[1,2]);
> z, r;
[ 4, 1 ] 2/3
> [(8/3)*r, (4/9)*r^2];      // docstring's claimed relation
[ 16/9, 16/81 ]              // != z
> [(8/3)*r^-1, (4/9)*r^-2];  // actual relation
[ 4, 1 ]                     // == z
findings.proposed_fix:
Line 842: change
{ Given a list of rational numbers v and a corresponding positive integer weights w, returns a list of integers z and a nonzero rational number r such that z[i] = v[i]*r^w[i] for all i.
to
{ Given a list of rational numbers v and a corresponding list of positive integer weights w, returns a list of integers z and a nonzero rational number r such that z[i] = v[i]*r^-w[i] for all i.
(Alternatively return 1/r, but callers in this file discard r, so fixing the docstring is the minimal change.)

findings.description: Docstring claims the intrinsic 'returns a sequence primes optionally followed by a sequence of composites'. Actually it always returns a SINGLE sorted sequence in which primes and composites are merged (line 823 appends the composite cofactor into the same list P), followed by a BOOLEAN that is true iff all entries are prime. The declared return signature (SeqEnum, SeqEnum) is also wrong for the second value.

The guard 'require Abs(n) gt 1: "Input must be nonzero"' is unreachable with default parameters: line 784 already returns for every |n| <= 10^mLimit (which covers 0 and +-1), so n=0 reaches Magma's Factorization(0) and produces a generic error instead of the intended require message; line 785 ('if Abs(n) eq 1 then return [], n; end if;') is dead code for the same reason (and is inconsistent with line 784, which returns Factorization(1) = [] with sign 1 rather than [],n). The zero check must come first.

Runtime error in 'Factorization': Argument 1 is not non-zero   // Magma's internal error, not the require message on line 786

findings.description: The finite-field branch and the generic branch of facpat use different multiplicity conventions although all four overloads carry the same docstring ('the factorization pattern of f'). Over a non-finite ring the pattern counts repeated factors with multiplicity ({* Degree(a[1])^^a[2] : a in Factorization(f) *}, line 762), but the finite-field branch (line 759-760) computes the pattern of the RADICAL: each distinct irreducible is counted once regardless of its exponent, because the &join over SquarefreeFactorization(f) ignores the multiplicity b[2]. Hence for non-squarefree f the multiset does not sum to deg f and disagrees with the generic overload on the same polynomial. Either the finite-field branch should weight by b[2] for consistency, or the docstrings should state the radical convention for finite fields (only matters for callers reducing at ramified primes; for squarefree inputs all branches agree, verified by random sweep).
findings.evidence:
> R<x> := PolynomialRing(Integers()); f := (x+1)^2*(x^2+x+7);
> facpat(f);      // generic branch, multiplicities counted
{* 1^^2, 2 *}
> facpat(f,5);    // f mod 5 = (x+1)^2*(irreducible quadratic): same shape, but
{* 1, 2 *}        // multiplicity of the repeated linear factor dropped (sum 3 != deg 4)
> facpat(f,3);    // f mod 3 = (x+1)^2*(x+2)^2
{* 1^^2 *}        // sum 2 != deg 4

findings.description: Docstring says 'returns the least integer n such the denominator of r/p^n is coprime to p'. The set of such n is unbounded below (it is an interval (-inf, v]), so there is no least element; the function returns the GREATEST such n, which is the correct generalization of the p-adic valuation to composite p. ('such the' is also a typo for 'such that'.)
findings.proposed_fix:
Line 831: change
{ Given a rational number r and a positive integer p returns the least integer n such the denominator of r/p^n is coprime to p.
to
{ Given a rational number r and a positive integer p returns the greatest integer n such that the denominator of r/p^n is coprime to p.

findings.description: The 'elif inv[4] ne 0' branch (lines 909-920) of the Fp normalization is mathematically unreachable for p > 2: Igusa invariants satisfy J8 = (J2*J6 - J4^2)/4, so J2 = J4 = J6 = 0 forces J8 = 0 in odd characteristic, and the p = 2 case returns earlier at line 891. Harmless dead code (confirmed by an exhaustive sweep of all quintics over GF(3),GF(5),GF(7),GF(11),GF(13): the first-nonzero-index distribution was [38648,3280,278,0,80] -- index 4 never occurs). Worth a comment, and it explains the copy-paste origin of the broken NormalizedIgusaClebschInvariants branch (which has one fewer invariant).
findings.evidence: Identity J8 = (J2*J6-J4^2)/4 (Igusa 1960; also LMFDB knowl g2c.igusa_invariants). Sweep over 42286 separable quintics over GF(p), p in {3,5,7,11,13}: no curve has J2=J4=J6=0 and J8 != 0.
findings.proposed_fix: No functional change needed; optionally add a comment '// unreachable for p>2 since 4*J8 = J2*J6-J4^2' above line 909.
